headline: US 'not serious' about talks, confused diplomacy with imposing demands
dek: 'The American side is not serious about negotiations,' Baqaei said at a news conference, as cited by state-run IRNA (via Anadolu, carried by Dawn). He said Washington repeatedly confused diplomacy with imposing demands on Tehran, recalled Trump expressing support for negotiations shortly before…
sources: Iran foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei, news conference, via IRNA as carried by Anadolu and Dawn
fault_line: Is Tehran negotiating in good faith while Washington plays for time, or is 'not serious' Tehran's excuse for keeping its preconditions while the strike clock runs?

sections.what_happened: 'The American side is not serious about negotiations,' Baqaei said at a news conference, as cited by state-run IRNA (via Anadolu, carried by Dawn). He said Washington repeatedly confused diplomacy with imposing demands on Tehran, recalled Trump expressing support for negotiations shortly before the June 2025 US military attacks on Iran ('What do you call this? Do you see any goodwill in this approach?'), and said Tehran has received no new European proposal beyond a political statement, criticising the UK, France and Germany for following Washington's lead on restoring UN sanctions and failing to condemn military attacks. This is Tehran's public line ON THE SAME DAY the Mecca Pact delegations met Iranian leaders in Tehran (record 1900-01): talks opened, and Tehran publicly says the other side is not serious.
sections.what_verified: One publisher family actually retrieved (Dawn, T3). Its underlying chain (Anadolu T3 STATE TR citing IRNA) was NOT independently retrieved this scan, so those do not count as additional families. The quote itself is Baqaei's on-record statement, accurately carried.
sections.what_disputed: Baqaei's 'not serious' charge is Tehran's position, not a verified fact about US intent; the US has not publicly responded to this specific charge in retrieved reporting. It sits alongside the same-day Tehran talks opening and the separate AJ report that Baqaei also said Iran 'never left negotiations' and communicates via intermediaries -- Tehran is signalling both openness and distrust at once. No US reply, no written proposal text retrieved.
sections.why_matters: The day the mediators arrived in Tehran, Tehran said the quiet part out loud: America is 'not serious' about talks -- and reminded everyone Trump talked peace days before the June bombs fell.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Dawn Oct 26 17:04 PKT = 16:04 , in no prior scan today) -- Iran FM spokesman Baqaei: US 'not serious' about talks, confused diplomacy with imposing demands

totw_analysis: Our read: The day the mediators arrived in Tehran, Tehran said the quiet part out loud: America is 'not serious' about talks -- and reminded everyone Trump talked peace days before the June bombs fell. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Tehran negotiating in good faith while Washington plays for time, or is 'not serious' Tehran's excuse for keeping its preconditions while the strike clock runs?
